fields.meta_title: Personal Training Intake Form Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a personal training intake form with goals, training history, available days, and a PAR-Q+ step, sent to the right trainer. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Personal Training Intake Form for the First Session
fields.hero_description: Build a personal training intake form that collects goals, available days, and PAR-Q+ answers before the first session.
fields.features_heading: What the Trainer Knows Before the First Rep
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the intake around the client's goal and schedule, and the screening answers stay inside the app.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the goal

A client who picks strength is asked which lifts they do now and how many days they train. Pick a race instead, and the form asks for the race date and weekly mileage.
fields.feature_2:
The PAR-Q+ as its own step

The first page of the official PAR-Q+ holds seven general health questions. A Yes to any of them opens the follow-up pages, and the client signs the declaration on screen.
fields.feature_3:
Available days, picked as checkboxes

Clients tick the mornings and evenings they can train, then request up to three time slots for session one. The trainer sees every request on one screen, by start date.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts that say an intake is ready

The trainer gets an email or a Slack message with the client's name and a note that the intake is ready. Screening answers stay out of the message and wait in the app.
fields.feature_5:
Client records in a database you own

Every intake is saved as a row in a database you own, searchable by client and by trainer. With no response caps, a month of heavy sign-ups runs through the same intake form.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take elsewhere

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository when the intake has to sit inside a member app you already run. Host it where you like and keep building.

fields.tab_content_1:
Seven No answers, and session one is requested

Corwin Kerrane signs up at Ironwhistle Strength. He picks strength as his goal, notes 2 years of lifting at a home gym, and answers No to all seven PAR-Q+ questions. He signs the declaration and requests Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday at 6 AM. Trainer Liesel Lartey gets an email that his intake is ready.
fields.tab_content_2:
Session one waits while a trainer reads one Yes

Gannet Fitness screens every new member with the PAR-Q+. Philippa Dulac answers Yes to one question on page 1, and the form opens the follow-up pages. Her intake reads Needs review, and her first session stays unbooked. Oskar Ferrante gets a Slack message that a new intake needs his review, with no answers in it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two dumbbells, one pull-up bar, no bench, all on file

Marisela Quill coaches clients by video, and her intake asks about home equipment. Bastian Greaves lists two adjustable dumbbells up to 50 lb and one pull-up bar, and checks No bench. He picks Monday and Wednesday at 7 PM for calls. Marisela reads the list the day before and plans a program with no bench work.
fields.tab_content_4:
One of four trainers fits fat loss after 6 PM

Wyncote Athletic Club has four trainers, and its intake asks every new member for a goal and a time slot. Henrietta Sowande picks fat loss and evenings after 6 PM. Dashiell Okoye is the one of the four who coaches fat loss in that slot, and her intake goes to him. He gets an email that it is ready and calls her the next day.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Personal Training Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a personal training intake form that screens each new client and sends the intake to the right trainer.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what the first session needs
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Give the PAR-Q+ its own page
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide what a Yes answer does
fields.howto_step_1_des: List what you need before a client walks in: the goal, how long they have trained and where, and the days they can come. Anything you would otherwise ask in the first 10 minutes of session one belongs on the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Copy the seven page 1 questions from the official PAR-Q+ at eparmedx.com word for word, since the site warns against outdated or modified copies. Put them on a page of their own and end it with the participation declaration and a signature.
fields.howto_step_3_des: A Yes on page 1 sends the client to the PAR-Q+ follow-up questions. Have the form open those pages after any Yes, and hold the first session until a trainer has read the intake and approved the booking.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick one person to own the review queue, ideally a qualified exercise professional. A Yes to any PAR-Q+ follow-up question sends the client to the ePARmed-X+ or a qualified exercise professional. Put that person's name on the review screen.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the goal list, the PAR-Q+ page, the Yes rule, and the reviewer into one prompt. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and a screen where trainers see new intakes. Change any question later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Map goals and time slots to trainers
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write a short table of which trainer coaches which goal at which times, and pick a backup for weeks someone is away. Each intake then goes to the trainer in the matching row, and their email names the client and nothing else.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Fill out the form as a made-up client
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit two test intakes from a phone: one with No to all seven questions and one with a single Yes. The first should request a session, the second should open the follow-up pages and wait for review, and both should land in the database.

faq_plan.q: What is a personal training intake form?
faq_plan.a: A personal training intake form is the questionnaire a new client fills out before the first session with a trainer. It records the client's goal, training history, and available days. It can also carry the PAR-Q+, a seven-question readiness screen, as a separate step with a signed declaration.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a personal training intake form?
faq_plan.a: Decide what a trainer needs before session one, where the PAR-Q+ goes, and what a Yes answer does. Put those choices in a single prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, which returns the form plus a table that stores each intake.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a personal training intake form ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with four groups: the client's goal, how long and where they have trained, the days and times they can come in, and the seven PAR-Q+ questions. Add questions that follow the goal, such as race date and weekly mileage for a runner. Cut anything the trainer would not read before session one.

faq_plan.q: How is a personal training intake form different from other client intake forms?
faq_plan.a: It screens for exercise readiness and plans a schedule. The PAR-Q+ and the client's training days carry most of the weight. Other intakes collect different things. An accounting client intake form, for example, asks for prior returns and income documents, with no health screen and no time slots.

faq_plan.q: What should a personal training intake form do after a yes on the health screening?
faq_plan.a: It should open the PAR-Q+ follow-up questions, which relate to living with a chronic medical condition, and mark the intake for review. The PAR-Q+ notes that healthcare clearance may be required for someone identified as higher risk, depending on the condition. Leave that call to the reviewer, and keep the booking button off the client's screen until then.

faq_plan.q: Can clients sign a personal training intake form online?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The PAR-Q+ asks the client to sign its participation declaration, and the app Emergent builds can capture that signature on screen at the end of the step. The signed intake is saved with the client's record, and nobody scans a paper copy into a folder.

faq_plan.q: Should goals on a personal training intake form be a list or open text?
faq_plan.a: Use a short list, plus one optional text box. A fixed list lets each goal open its own questions and send the intake to the trainer who coaches it. A life coaching intake form can leave goals open-ended, because nothing downstream depends on the exact answer.

faq_plan.q: How often should clients update their personal training intake form?
faq_plan.a: Ask for a fresh intake when a client's goal changes, after a long break from training, or when their health changes. Set a yearly reminder as a floor. Keep each version as its own dated record. A trainer can then compare what the client said last time with what changed.

faq_plan.q: Can a personal training intake form collect home equipment for online clients?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask about each piece as its own question: the heaviest dumbbell, whether they own a pull-up bar, and whether they own a bench. A coach planning by video then knows which exercises are possible before the first call. A form Emergent builds saves every intake to a database you own, next to the client's earlier records.

faq_plan.q: Can a personal training intake form send clients to different trainers?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Use the goal and the requested time slot to pick the trainer, and send each intake only to that person. The same routing works on a project request form that assigns work by type. Forms Emergent builds have no response caps, and a January rush of sign-ups runs through the same rules.
